evidence.positive:
Reproduced the ticket's exact scenario against the running app (demo-demo): created an ADULT patient with recorded weight 36.9 kg, started the case via POST /api/app-launch, injected a vecuronium bolus 30 min prior via POST /api/admin/bolus/patient/{pmrn}/{caseId}, recorded TOF=2 via POST /api/admin/observations/..., then called POST /api/cds/medication-selection/{pmrn}/{caseId} with m-sugammadex as loopuser. The rule w-sugammadex-default-dose fired with details {"WEIGHT_KG":36.9,"TOF":2,"CITATION_ID":"r-sugammadex-dose-2"} -- the same details map quoted in the ticket -- and the INTRAVENOUS dose options came back as {"amt":"75","def":true,"calc":"2 mg/kg x 36.9 kg (recorded weight)
=73.8 mg, rounded to the nearest 25 mg
~75 mg"}, plus 150 mg (4 mg/kg) and 600 mg (16 mg/kg), each annotated "rounded to the nearest 25 mg". No unrounded 73.8 mg option appears alongside the 75 mg one. Separately exercised the 16 mg/kg branch: a 36.9 kg adult given 60 mg rocuronium 2 min before selection got citation r-sugammadex-dose-16 and a default of 600 mg (590.4 rounded to the nearest 25 mg).
evidence.negative: Same flow with an adult at 45 kg: the response kept the medication's configured 50 mg factor -- options 100 mg (default, "=90 mg, rounded to the nearest 50 mg"), 200 mg, 700 mg -- with no 25 mg step anywhere and no 75/150/600 values. Ran the exact 40 kg boundary too: 80 mg -> "rounded to the nearest 50 mg" -> 100 mg, so the 25 mg step starts strictly below 40 kg. Also ran a PEDIATRIC 30 kg patient: the rule abstained ("Rule evaluated: w-sugammadex-default-dose -> false No rounding factor defined for SUGAMMADEX" in the app log) and the options stayed unrounded at 60/120/180 mg, confirming the 25 mg step does not leak onto pediatric patients. The 45 kg high-rocuronium case likewise kept the 50 mg step (720 -> 700 mg).
evidence.red_check:
Compiled the parent commit's (efe9dc30e) TOFSugammadexAdjustmentWarningRule.java inside the app container with javac against /app/jib-classpath-file (de-lombok'd the @Slf4j logger; added one log.error carrying the computed default dose so the wrong value is visible in the log), backed up the shipped class (md5 2827c914ee6fbdad6bd76b681385b35a), swapped the pre-fix class into /app/classes and restarted the container. Re-running the identical 36.9 kg / TOF 2 selection then returned the bug exactly as the ticket describes: default option {"amt":"73.8","def":true,"calc":"2 mg/kg x 36.9 kg (recorded weight)
=73.8 mg"} with no rounding clause, and sibling options 147.6 mg and 590.4 mg. The log line OR2805-REDCHECK-PREFIX-DEFAULT-DOSE=73.8 was emitted. Restored the backed-up class, restarted, verified the md5 matches the original byte for byte, and re-ran the positive case: 75 mg / "rounded to the nearest 25 mg" is back.

caveats: Exercised only the demo-demo sugammadex config (weightRoundingFactor 50 mg, adult options 2/4/16 mg/kg); Mayo's config and its single-dose/simplified-TOF rule variants were not run.
Validated at the API layer (POST /api/cds/medication-selection response), not through the browser dosing form, so how the rounded options render in the UI was not observed.
The TOF=4 ratio path that yields 0.22 mg/kg (a sub-25 mg product that should round up to 25 mg) was not exercised against the running app; only unit tests cover it.
The red check swapped the rule class only -- DoseOptionDTO stayed at the fixed version, which is behaviour-neutral for the pre-fix rule since it calls the unchanged fromWeightBasedDoseOption path.
Pediatric sugammadex in demo has no rounding factor, so the rule abstains there; the pediatric arm of the underweight check could not be reached in this tenant.

automation.assessment: The merged commit already carries strong unit coverage: seven tests in TOFSugammadexAdjustmentWarningRuleTest (underweight default dose, TOF 0, 40 kg boundary, pediatric, 16 mg/kg, sub-25 mg round-up, option-list parity) and one in DosingFormStateTest for the merged form state. Those lock in the arithmetic and the option de-duplication, so nothing needs re-writing at the unit level. What is not covered anywhere is the wire contract -- that the rounded options and the 25 mg annotation actually survive into the medication-selection response a clinician's client consumes. That is the gap worth a qa-suite supplemental test.
proposed_tests: qa-suite supplemental: 36.9 kg adult with prior vecuronium and TOF 2 selecting sugammadex returns dose options 75/150/600 mg, the 75 mg option flagged default, each annotated 'rounded to the nearest 25 mg'.
qa-suite supplemental: assert absence -- the same response contains no 73.8/147.6/590.4 mg option, so the unrounded and rounded doses are never offered side by side.
qa-suite supplemental: 45 kg adult in the same scenario keeps the configured 50 mg step (100/200/700 mg), guarding the 40 kg threshold from regressing.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: A 36.9 kg adult with prior vecuronium and TOF 2 now gets a default sugammadex dose of 75 mg, shown as 73.8 mg rounded to the nearest 25 mg, with the 4 and 16 mg/kg options rounded to 150 and 600 mg on the same step.
Negative: A 45 kg adult, and an adult at exactly 40 kg, keep the configured 50 mg step, and a pediatric patient is untouched.
Red check: Swapping the pre-fix rule class into the running container brought back the unrounded 73.8 mg default and the 147.6 and 590.4 mg options, then the shipped class was restored and the 75 mg result confirmed.

Automation: Unit coverage for the rounding already merged with the fix; a supplemental qa-suite test is proposed to lock the rounded options into the medication-selection response.
